To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

GP can discover better similarity functions for text classification, that these functions can be used in combination with other classification techniques to improve classification accuracy, and that GP is superior to other fusion techniques in discovering better similarity functions for classification.

(1) GP is able to discover similarity functions superior in classification performance to those based on a single type or a combination of types of evidence; (2) GP-based similarity functions outperform Support Vector Machine classifiers; and (3) GP-based similarity fusion is better than linear fusion.

GP techniques are able to discover superior similarity functions for text classification and that the effectiveness of the similarity functions can be improved by fusing citation- and content-based measures of similarity.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the problem of combining different types of information for text classification and shows that the fusion of different types of evidence can lead to improved classification performance.
the problem of text classification and the fusion of different measures of similarity.
the development of a framework for the automatic discovery of similarity functions for text classification using citation information and structural evidence.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the fusion of citation- and structural-based evidence using Genetic Programming is a viable approach to improve classification effectiveness.
the fusion of structural and citational evidence through GP is superior to other fusion techniques.
the GP approach to fusion is a promising technique for text categorization.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
GP is a promising technique to discover the best fusion of different types of evidence for text classification tasks.
GP techniques are effective in discovering similarity functions superior to other fusion techniques.
the GP-based fusion of structural and bibliometric information can improve classification effectiveness.
The main takeaway from our work is that
GP can be used as a general purpose tool for discovering effective fusion functions.
GP can be used for automatic fusion of evidence from different types of information to improve text classification.
the fusion framework based on GP is an effective approach to combine the citation and structural evidence for text classification.
